confidence_notes: Two web searches were used for food and drink prices. Seattle sources (Numbeo data via Expatica, Wise, Citycost, Expatistan, Mylifeelsewhere and a 2026 dining guide) put an inexpensive meal at $21–25, a cappuccino at $6.30–7.00 and a draft beer of about a pint or half-litre at around $8 ($6–12). A mid-range dinner for two without drinks is put at $100–130, depending on how tax and service fees are counted. No combined sourced figures were found for cocktail or wine prices. Those two are estimates based on how drink prices usually compare with beer in Seattle, so they are less certain. All four accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge only. I did not check booking sites or live listings. They are set for July, which is Seattle's peak summer and cruise season. Seattle has few registered hostels, so the hostel anchors are especially uncertain. July 2026 accommodation prices may also be pushed up by FIFA World Cup matches in Seattle.
comparable_city_reasoning: Prices are at a high-cost US West Coast level, similar to San Francisco and Portland. Restaurant prices are a bit below San Francisco. Summer hotel rates are similar to other major US cities with strong tourist demand.
